To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phase locking is equivalent to the stability of an auxiliary linearized system, the number of slipped periods is bounded by the number of unstable equilibria, and the set of possible frequencies is a union of intervals, each of which is determined by an auxiliary linearized problem.

the number of slipped cycle is bounded from above by the number of the first unstable equilibrium and the possible frequencies of periodic solutions are given by the frequencies of the first unstable equilibria.

(i) the phase-locked solution is the one which minimizes the integral quadratic constraint, (ii) the transient process is bounded by a number of cycles, and (iii) the possible frequencies of periodic solutions are bounded by a certain function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
a new mathematical theory of synchronization systems, which is based on the theory of integral quadratic constraints.
the analysis of synchronization systems, which are nonlinear systems with a linear dynamic part, and a periodic non-linearity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the considered class of synchronization systems, the number of cycle slips is bounded, the number of possible periodic solutions is finite and the number of possible frequencies is finite, as well.

the method of integral quadratics, in its various forms, provides a useful and efficient tool for analysis of synchronization systems, including phase locking, oscillations (periodic and quasi-periodic) and cycle slippings.

, for a given synchronization system with a prescribed periodic nonlinearity, the phase-locked solutions are those which satisfy a set of linear constraints, while the possible oscillations are those which satisfy the same constraints with the additional condition that their frequency is an integer multiple of the nonlinearity period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we offer a new, more efficient and general approach for the analysis of synchronization systems, which can also be applied to other classes of nonlinear systems, e.g., systems with aperiodic nonlinearities, such as sampled-data systems.
the method of integral constraints allows one to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stability of synchronization systems.

the proposed methods allow one to obtain explicit estimates for the phase-locking time, cycle slipping and periodic oscillations in synchronization systems, based on a single scalar function of a linear dynamic block.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given system, it is often possible to obtain a priori estimates of the number of slipped oscillatory cycles and the frequency of the oscillation.

, in the presence of a periodic nonlinearty, the convergence of solutions is determined by a single parameter, namely the “frequency ratio” between the linear and nonlinear parts of the synchronization system.
the mentioned three problems can be treated in a unified framework, based on the same set of tools.
